key_insight: A lightweight, on-device Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) built around a Temporal Convolutional Network keeps EMG gesture recognition accurate under real-world signal drift without heavy retraining or large datasets.
problem_solved: Mitigates sharp performance degradation of EMG-based gesture classifiers caused by electrode shifts, muscle fatigue, and posture changes, while avoiding costly offline re-training and high-compute adaptation pipelines that are impractical for energy-constrained wearables.
method: Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) backbone tailored to temporal EMG patterns.
A compact, low-cost TTA module that adapts model parameters or normalization statistics at test time using only unlabeled incoming signals.
Architecture and update rules optimized for minimal compute and memory so adaptation can run on battery-powered wearable devices.
impact: Makes long-term, reliable EMG decoding feasible on resource-constrained wearables, improving user experience and reducing maintenance/retraining needs; offers ML practitioners a practical path to deploy adaptive models in the wild.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sensor → TCN model → lightweight on-device TTA loop → updated predictions
Before vs. after line chart: accuracy over time demonstrating sharp drop without TTA and stability with TTA
Bar chart comparing compute, memory, and energy of the proposed TTA vs. full re-training and other baselines
Illustration of real-world drift sources (electrode shift, fatigue, posture) linked to model performance
paper_title: Lightweight Test-Time Adaptation for EMG-Based Gesture Recognition
paper_authors: Nia Touko, Matthew O A Ellis, Cristiano Capone, Alessio Burrello, Elisa Donati
